# US-01.4 — Keep credentials out of version control

|                  |                                                                                |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Epic**         | [EPIC-01 Foundation & Environment](../epics/EPIC-01-foundation-environment.md) |
| **Priority**     | **P0**                                                                         |
| **Estimate**     | 1                                                                              |
| **Status**       | In progress                                                                    |
| **Owning agent** | `story-builder`                                                                |
| **Files**        | [.gitignore](../../../.gitignore)                                              |

## User story

**As a** team publishing this repository for a hackathon submission,
**I want** credentials and generated artefacts excluded from version control from the very first commit,
**so that** we never leak a project secret and never have to rewrite git history to remove one.

## Why this is P0

A leaked `.env` or service-account key is not a bug you fix later. Once it is in a public repository's history, the credential is compromised and must be rotated. [EPIC-09](../epics/EPIC-09-demo-submission.md) makes this repository public — this story must close before the first commit, not before the submission.

## Acceptance criteria

**AC1 — Secrets excluded**
Given the repository is initialised,
when I run `git check-ignore .env`,
then `.env` is reported as ignored. The same holds for `credentials.json`, `*-key.json`, `*.pem`, `*.p12`.

**AC2 — Template not excluded**
Given a `.env.example` exists,
then it is **not** ignored, so new developers still get a template.

**AC3 — Build artefacts excluded**
Then `venv/`, `__pycache__/`, `.pytest_cache/`, `.coverage`, `coverage.json`, and `data_samples/` are all ignored.

**AC4 — Reports retained**
Then `agile/backlog.json` and `agile/reports/` are **not** ignored — sprint history is a deliverable, not an artefact.

**AC5 — Clean status**
Given a configured working environment,
when I run `git status`,
then no `.env` and no credential file appears as tracked or untracked-but-stageable.

**AC6 — Clean history**
Given the repository is about to be made public,
when history is inspected,
then no commit contains a secret.

## Tasks

- [x] Write `.gitignore` covering secrets, Python artefacts, coverage output, and generated samples
- [x] Negate `.env.example` so the template survives
- [ ] **Run `git init`** — until the repository exists, `.gitignore` is an inert text file
- [ ] Confirm `git check-ignore -v .env` reports a match
- [ ] Run `git status` and confirm nothing sensitive is listed
- [ ] Create a `.env.example` with the key names and empty values

## Current state

`.gitignore` is written and correct. **This directory is not a git repository**, so none of it is in force:

```
$ git check-ignore -q .env
fatal: not a git repository (or any of the parent directories): .git
```

Every protective claim in this story is currently unverifiable. `./setup_gcp.sh` writes a real `.env` containing a live project ID — if `git init` happens after that file exists and someone runs `git add .`, the secret is committed on the first commit.

Run `git init` before anything else in this epic.

## Test cases

Verified by shell assertion rather than pytest.

| Case                                         | Expectation              |
| -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------ |
| `git check-ignore -q .env`                   | exit 0 (ignored)         |
| `git check-ignore -q credentials.json`       | exit 0                   |
| `git check-ignore -q venv/lib`               | exit 0                   |
| `git check-ignore -q coverage.json`          | exit 0                   |
| `git check-ignore -q .env.example`           | exit 1 (**not** ignored) |
| `git check-ignore -q agile/backlog.json`     | exit 1 (**not** ignored) |
| `git status --porcelain \| grep -c '\.env$'` | 0                        |

## Definition of done

The repository is initialised, every assertion above holds, and `git log -p` contains no secret.

## Related guardrails

Agent-side protection already exists and complements this story — the `guard-secrets` hook denies any tool access to `.env` and credential files and blocks commands that would print tokens. That protects against the agent; `.gitignore` protects against a human running `git add .`. Both are needed.
